forces.title: Persistent delays in IBC resolution and liquidation timelines constrain efficiency
forces.description: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) resolution and liquidation timelines remain elevated, with average resolution time increasing to 757 days and nearly three-fourths of ongoing CIRPs exceeding 270 days as of June 2026. Liquidation cases averaged 540 days, with almost 70% pending for over two years. These prolonged delays are attributed to aging cases, litigation, procedural bottlenecks, and challenges in attracting resolution applicants, significantly hampering recovery efficiency and value maximisation.
forces.source_title: IBC Recovery Gains Momentum in Q1FY27, Despite Continued Delays

forces.title: Liquidation dominates IBC exit routes, indicating severe financial stress
forces.description: Liquidation continues to be the dominant closure route for Corporate Insolvency Resolution Processes (CIRPs), accounting for 33.5% of admitted cases as of Q1FY27. This persistence suggests that a significant proportion of companies enter the insolvency process after substantial deterioration in their financial and operational positions, limiting the feasibility of revival through resolution plans. While IBC creates value over liquidation, the high liquidation rate points to challenges in preserving stressed businesses as going concerns and constrains overall recovery potential.
forces.source_title: IBC Recovery Gains Momentum in Q1FY27, Despite Continued Delays

forces.title: Regulatory amendments enhance IBC transparency and efficiency for faster resolutions
forces.description: The IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026, has introduced significant regulatory changes to improve transparency, strengthen information flows, and enhance the efficiency of insolvency proceedings. Key amendments include simplified default recognition, standardised disputed default frameworks, enhanced disclosure for pre-packaged processes, and stronger claim verification. These reforms are expected to improve the quality and availability of information at earlier stages, reduce disputes, facilitate quicker creditor decision-making, and strengthen oversight, supporting faster resolutions and better value realisation over the medium term.
forces.source_title: IBC Recovery Gains Momentum in Q1FY27, Despite Continued Delays

forces.title: Subdued fresh CIRP admissions indicate normalisation rather than deterioration
forces.description: Fresh Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) admissions remained subdued in Q1FY27, with 177 cases admitted, down 5.3% year-on-year. This trend, alongside stable ongoing cases, suggests that case closures have largely kept pace with fresh inflows, preventing a material build-up of pending cases. Financial creditors continue to drive the majority of new filings (65.5% in Q1FY27), reinforcing their reliance on IBC. The subdued admissions indicate a normalisation in new stress rather than a broad deterioration in corporate financial health.
forces.source_title: IBC Recovery Gains Momentum in Q1FY27, Despite Continued Delays

forces.title: India's debt ecosystem is shallow and bank-dominated, hindering market-based financing
forces.description: India’s debt ecosystem is characterised by a structurally shallow and bank-dominated financial system, with bank credit to GDP significantly lower than Asian peers and the corporate bond market representing only about 16% of GDP. Corporate bonds account for roughly 21% of the total debt market, underscoring heavy reliance on government securities and bank financing. This structural imbalance points to constrained capital market depth, limiting the role of market-based financing compared to more advanced economies and impacting long-term growth.

forces.title: Corporate bond market concentrated in high ratings and lacks secondary liquidity
forces.description: India's corporate bond market remains heavily skewed towards highly rated instruments (AAA and AA categories account for over 85%) due to investment mandates for institutional investors like insurance companies and pension funds. This limits depth in lower-rated segments. Furthermore, the secondary market suffers from limited liquidity, with G-secs dominating turnover (10 times that of corporate bonds) and a low corporate bond ADTO as a percentage of outstanding stock, hindering efficient price discovery and investor confidence.

forces.title: Regulatory measures and tax reforms to deepen corporate bond market
forces.description: Continued regulatory and policy reforms are aimed at deepening India's corporate bond market. Proposals include rationalising adverse taxation on debt holdings, reducing TDS burdens, and boosting secondary market liquidity through market making and bond derivatives. Broadening the investor base via increased awareness, relaxed investment mandates for retirement funds/insurers, and simplified FPI regulations, along with strengthening market borrowing frameworks for large issuers, are expected to enhance market depth, transparency, and participation, supporting long-term growth.

forces.title: Robust credit demand and investor appetite drive securitisation market resilience
forces.description: The retail asset securitisation market demonstrates resilience, recording Rs 59,000 crore in Q1FY27 (13% y-o-y growth). This momentum is driven by healthy credit demand, sustained investor appetite, and originators' focus on diversifying funding. Gold loans have emerged as a key asset class, and improving industry conditions combined with demand for priority-sector lending assets have boosted MFI-backed securitisation. These factors underline the sector's strength and potential for continued growth in FY27.
forces.source_title: Q1FY27 Retail Securitisation at Rs 59,000 Cr

forces.title: RBI's ECL framework poses capital pressure for banks from forward-looking provisioning
forces.description: The Reserve Bank of India’s Expected Credit Loss (ECL) framework, effective April 2027, mandates forward-looking provisioning for banks. This regulatory change is expected to put greater capital pressure, particularly on Public Sector Banks (PSUs) and mid-sized private banks with thinner overlays compared to larger, well-capitalised peers. The transition will require banks to adjust their provisioning models and capital planning, potentially impacting their capacity for credit expansion and their participation in fixed income markets.
forces.source_title: Indian Banking Sector: Top Updates: Banking Sector RoundUp - FY26

forces.title: Growing global integration of EM bond markets, including India, attracts FPIs
forces.description: Emerging market (EM) bond markets are experiencing growing global integration, evident in the increasing inclusion of EM local currency bonds in major global benchmark indices. India's inclusion in the JPMorgan GBI-EM Global Diversified Index (June 2024), Bloomberg's EM Local Currency Index (Jan 2025), and FTSE Russell EM Government Bond Index (Sep 2025) marks a significant milestone. This trend is expected to support substantial passive foreign portfolio investment (FPI) inflows, enhancing the structural depth and liquidity of India's domestic bond market.
forces.source_title: Structural Shifts in Debt Market: Emerging Themes

forces.title: Rising capital market yields drive credit substitution towards bank lending
forces.description: Rising capital market yields have significantly altered borrowing dynamics, tightening financial conditions through market channels faster than through bank lending rates. This divergence, particularly with a relatively flat yield curve and higher short-term rates, encourages corporates and NBFCs to substitute bond and money-market borrowing with bank credit. While AAA issuers maintain some bond cost advantage, A-rated issuers now find NCD funding more expensive than bank loans, leading to a shift in funding patterns, with NCD issuances significantly declining in FY26.
forces.source_title: Yield Driven Credit Substitution Favours Bank Lending

forces.title: Shift to bank credit concentrates risk and reduces tenor diversification
forces.description: The increased shift from bond markets to bank credit, while easing near-term refinancing and supporting liquidity for stronger entities, introduces new risks. This trend brings lower tenor diversification and greater exposure to floating rates for borrowers. For banks, it concentrates credit and duration risk on their balance sheets, potentially pressuring returns if lending rates lag funding costs. This divergence in market and bank transmission suggests stress may be deferred rather than absorbed, with key risks depending on funding stability and leverage.
forces.source_title: Yield Driven Credit Substitution Favours Bank Lending

forces.title: RBI eases capital requirements for banks by dissolving IFR and including quarterly profits
forces.description: The RBI has proposed key regulatory changes to ease capital requirements for banks, including the dissolution of the Investment Fluctuation Reserve (IFR) and permitting banks to include quarterly profits in capital adequacy calculations. The inclusion of IFR into CET1 capital is expected to improve ratios by 26-31 bps across banks, reducing locked-in reserves. While this boosts core capital, it mandates banks to strengthen internal risk management for mark-to-market (MTM) shocks, promoting more stable capital reporting and risk absorption.
forces.source_title: RBI Measures to Ease Capital Requirements for Banks

forces.title: InvIT AUM growth driven by investor appetite and infrastructure institutionalisation
forces.description: Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) in India have seen significant growth, with AUM doubling from ~Rs 3.0 lakh crore in FY22 to ~Rs 6.25 lakh crore by FY25. This expansion is driven by strong structural investor appetite and the rapid institutionalisation of operational infrastructure platforms. CareEdge Ratings expects InvIT AUM to grow by an additional ~Rs 1 lakh crore during FY26, supported by portfolio expansion across roads, transmission, warehousing, and renewable sectors, and the robust National Monetisation Pipeline-II.
forces.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

forces.title: InvIT AUM concentration in few sectors limits diversification opportunities
forces.description: Despite significant growth in India's InvIT AUM, market concentration remains a key concern, with telecom (~Rs 3.06 lakh crore) and roads (~Rs 2.46 lakh crore) together accounting for nearly 90% of the industry’s AUM as of March 31, 2025. This heavy concentration in just two segments signals a lack of sectoral diversification. While strong growth is projected, expanding into other infrastructure areas is crucial to reduce concentration risk and unlock broader market potential for InvIT debt structures.
forces.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

viewpoints.title: IBC framework shows Q1FY27 recovery momentum despite persistent resolution delays
viewpoints.description: CareEdge notes that the IBC framework demonstrated its effectiveness in Q1FY27, with recovery outcomes improving sequentially to 28.6% of admitted claims, significantly above liquidation values. Successful resolutions are increasing, and case inventory is stable, indicating ecosystem maturity. However, operational efficiency remains a principal challenge as resolution and liquidation timelines continue to increase due to complex and aging cases, constraining value maximisation.
viewpoints.source_title: IBC Recovery Gains Momentum in Q1FY27, Despite Continued Delays

viewpoints.title: IBC regulatory amendments to enhance transparency and efficiency for improved outcomes
viewpoints.description: CareEdge views the recent IBC (Amendment) Act, 2026, as positive, aiming to improve transparency, information quality, and process efficiency. Key changes like simplified default recognition, enhanced disclosures for pre-packaged processes, and stronger claim verification are expected to reduce disputes and facilitate quicker creditor decision-making. Effective implementation could lead to faster resolutions, better value realisation, and improved recovery outcomes over the medium term.
viewpoints.source_title: IBC Recovery Gains Momentum in Q1FY27, Despite Continued Delays

viewpoints.title: Indian debt capital market remains shallow and bank-dominated, hindering growth financing
viewpoints.description: CareEdge identifies India’s debt ecosystem as structurally shallow and bank-dominated, with bank credit significantly outpacing corporate bonds relative to GDP. The corporate bond market is underdeveloped in scale and participation, accounting for only about 16% of GDP, much lower than major global economies. This structural imbalance limits market-based financing, reinforcing a preference for bank-led intermediation and posing challenges for financing India's long-term growth aspirations.

viewpoints.title: A-rated corporate bonds present attractive risk-reward for investors due to high yields
viewpoints.description: CareEdge highlights that A-rated corporate papers offer a healthy risk-reward opportunity for investors. Despite low default risk, as reflected by high stability ratios, these papers command significant premiums over G-sec rates, with yields 280-330 basis points higher than similar-tenor triple-A papers, while maximum credit risk is below 20 bps. This suggests that current bond yields are influenced more by liquidity and investor awareness than by actual credit risk.

viewpoints.title: Retail asset securitisation market to maintain steady growth in FY27
viewpoints.description: CareEdge anticipates steady growth in the retail asset securitisation market for FY27, building on strong Q1FY27 volumes of Rs 59,000 crore. This positive outlook is driven by NBFCs' continued reliance on securitisation for funding, robust credit demand, and healthy investor appetite. Key contributors include gold loan financiers, and improving investor confidence in stable pool performance is boosting microfinance-backed PTC issuances, signaling sustained market momentum.
viewpoints.source_title: Q1FY27 Retail Securitisation at Rs 59,000 Cr

viewpoints.title: Easing bank margin pressure expected to sustain credit momentum in FY27
viewpoints.description: BCG projects that margin pressure for banks will ease in FY27, supported by stabilizing interest rates, declining funding costs, and deposit repricing. This environment is expected to support sustained credit growth. Furthermore, Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) remain well-capitalized with strong CRAR, providing a buffer for credit expansion and risk absorption, which indirectly supports the broader debt market through healthy financial intermediaries.
viewpoints.source_title: Indian Banking Sector: Top Updates: Banking Sector RonudUp - 9MFY26

viewpoints.title: India's corporate bond market underdeveloped but offers deepening opportunities
viewpoints.description: CareEdge asserts that India's corporate bond market is underdeveloped, overshadowed by bank lending and government securities, with low GDP penetration. However, the report also identifies significant opportunities to deepen the market through regulatory reforms, broadening issuer and investor bases, and improving liquidity. Furthermore, it highlights the potential for greater participation in mid- and lower-rated bonds, which offer attractive risk-reward profiles, if structural issues are addressed.
viewpoints.source_title: Indian Debt Capital Market - Can it Finance India's Growth?

viewpoints.title: Bond market crucial for India's USD 30 trillion economy vision by 2047
viewpoints.description: CareEdge emphasizes the pivotal role of a deep, resilient, and diversified financial system, especially the bond market, for India to achieve its 'Viksit Bharat' vision and become a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047. This is essential for supporting large-scale, long-term investments in critical sectors and for efficient capital allocation, especially given global uncertainties and the need to reduce reliance on bank financing.
viewpoints.source_title: Structural Shifts in Debt Market: Emerging Themes

viewpoints.title: India's government securities market improving but still faces structural gaps
viewpoints.description: CareEdge notes that India's government securities market has undergone structural and institutional improvements, with active debt management, shifts in investor composition, and increasing global integration. Despite positives like a well-diversified maturity profile and limited rollover risks, significant gaps persist, including limited retail and foreign investor participation, lower secondary-market trading volumes, and underdeveloped sub-sovereign debt markets, which need to be addressed for global alignment.
viewpoints.source_title: Structural Shifts in Debt Market: Emerging Themes

viewpoints.title: Yield-driven credit substitution favors bank lending over bond markets amid rising rates
viewpoints.description: CareEdge observes that rising capital market yields have tightened financial conditions faster than bank lending rates, leading corporates and NBFCs to substitute bond and money-market borrowing with bank credit. While AAA and AA issuers retain some cost advantage in bonds, the differential has narrowed significantly. For A-rated issuers, bond borrowing has become costlier than bank loans, indicating a shift in funding preferences driven by market volatility and repricing dynamics.
viewpoints.source_title: Yield Driven Credit Substitution Favours Bank Lending

viewpoints.title: Indian securitisation market fundamentals remain strong, anticipating sustained growth
viewpoints.description: CareEdge asserts that the fundamentals of the Indian securitisation market are robust, expecting continued growth in FY27 and beyond, despite a dip in retail volumes in FY26. This positive outlook is underpinned by strong domestic demand, resilient growth, improving investor confidence, and robust pool performance. PTC transactions are expected to remain preferred, with increasing investor acceptance of diversified retail asset classes like microfinance, gold loans, and unsecured loans.
viewpoints.source_title: FY26 Retail Securitisation at Rs 2.53 Trillion, First Dip Post-Pandemic

viewpoints.title: RBI measures to ease capital requirements positive for banks' core capital ratios
viewpoints.description: CareEdge views RBI's proposed changes—dissolution of the Investment Fluctuation Reserve (IFR) and allowing quarterly profits in capital adequacy calculations—as positive. These measures are expected to improve banks' core capital ratios by 26-31 bps and lead to more stable capital reporting. By reducing locked-in reserves, banks gain flexibility, although they will need to strengthen internal risk management for mark-to-market shocks in volatile interest rate environments.
viewpoints.source_title: RBI Measures to Ease Capital Requirements for Banks

viewpoints.title: InvIT AUM poised for significant growth in FY26, driven by infrastructure expansion
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings projects substantial growth for InvIT AUM in FY26, expecting an increase of approximately Rs 1 lakh crore. This positive trajectory is attributed to portfolio expansion in roads, transmission, warehousing, and renewable sectors, further boosted by the strong National Monetisation Pipeline-II (NMP-II). The growth reflects sustained investor appetite and the institutionalisation of infrastructure platforms, despite current AUM concentration in telecom and roads.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

viewpoints.title: IBC framework shows stabilisation, but persistent delays remain a key concern
viewpoints.description: CareEdge states that while the IBC framework remains central to India’s insolvency resolution, trends in Q4FY26 indicate stabilisation rather than sharp improvement. CIRP admissions moderated, and ongoing cases remained stable, showing some improvement in closures. However, delays in both resolution and liquidation processes persist as a key concern, with a significant majority of cases pending beyond prescribed timelines, affecting recovery efficiency and value realisation.
viewpoints.source_title: Fresh Admissions Ease in FY26, While Delays Continue in Existing Cases
